decision: Adam, 25 October 2026: isochrone fits for hosts without Gaia FLAME or TIC mass and radius.
method: isoclassify grid mode (Huber et al. 2017) with the inputs of Berger et al. (2020): MIST grid, Combined19 3D dust map (Bovy et al. 2016; Zenodo 3566060), Gaia DR3 parallax with the Lindegren et al. (2021) zero point, Gaia G/BP/RP, 2MASS JHKs and Pan-STARRS1 griz transformed to SDSS (Tonry et al. 2012). Rules declared before fitting in isochrones/build_inputs.py and review.py.
rule:
Review isoclassify grid solutions against the rule declared before fitting; write the solutions apply_isochrone uses.

review.py INPUT_CSV OUTPUT_CSV SOLUTIONS_JSON. Declared 26 October 2026 before any fit: a solution is used when mass,
radius and Teff are finite and the half 16-84 intervals of mass and radius are at most 25% of their medians; other hosts
stay held as unconstrained. Errors are the half 16-84 intervals. GSP-Phot Teff is compared descriptively.
Version 2 (26 October 2026, after the second pass returned 0.6-0.9% mass and radius errors for one host): the adopted
errors add the model-systematic floors of Tayar et al. (2022) in quadrature, 5% in mass, 4% in radius and 2% in Teff.
The acceptance rule still uses the statistical half-intervals, so the set of solved hosts does not change.

scope: Host stellar properties for V3 cases held for missing mass and radius. A solution replaces only that missing input; native fits, campaigns and closeouts run unchanged.
version_note: Version 2 adds the Tayar et al. (2022) model-systematic floors (5% mass, 4% radius, 2% Teff) in quadrature to the statistical half-intervals, after the second pass returned 0.6-0.9% errors for one host. The acceptance rule and the set of solved hosts are unchanged. Six queued pass-1 cases that had not started their native fits were re-planned with version 2 (previous plans in plan-superseded-*); the one pass-1 case already fitted (Gaia DR3 2078783726253023360) kept version 1, whose errors already exceeded the floors.

neighbours.note: Adam, 26 October 2026: incorporate strong single-star signals. The same rules fit capable scene neighbours that lack stellar properties for strong (search S/N >= 15) held signals; only Gaia DR3 2080571326002191488 (KIC 10286954's neighbour, 8.8 arcsec, parallax S/N 6.9) qualified. The other strong cases' neighbours are G 17-21 within 1-10 arcsec without BP/RP and with parallax S/N below 5.
